Massive Cleanliness Drive Conducted Along Sevagram Road
Monday, 06 April 2026
1245 Hits
In a remarkable display of collective responsibility and community spirit, the staff, students, faculty members, and sanitation workers of the Mahatma Gandhi Institute of Medical Sciences carried out an extensive cleanliness drive on 05
th
April 2026. As part of the ongoing
Swachhata Pakhwada
—a nationwide cleanliness initiative by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare—the particpants carried out an extensive cleanliness drive on Sunday morning along the main road outside the hospital premises.
The drive covered a significant stretch from the hospital’s main gate up to Sevagram Chowk, with both sides of the road being thoroughly cleaned. Beginning early in the morning, participants actively engaged in removing plastic waste, bottles, wrappers and other garbage that had accumulated along the roadside.
The initiative witnessed enthusiastic participation across all sections of the institute, reflecting a shared commitment towards environmental responsibility and public health. Equipped with gloves, garbage bags and collection truck, the volunteers worked towards restoring cleanliness to the area.
A notable outcome of the drive was the collection of nearly one tractor full of plastic waste, highlighting both the scale of the effort and the pressing need for sustained awareness regarding waste disposal practices.
“This cleanliness activity not only improved the immediate surroundings of the hospital but also served as a strong message to the public about the importance of maintaining hygiene in shared spaces. The institute reaffirmed its commitment to promoting cleanliness, environmental consciousness, and community engagement through such initiatives”, said Dr BS Garg (Secretary, Kasturba Health Society)
“The drive reinforces the role of healthcare institutions beyond clinical services—towards building a healthier and cleaner society”, said Dr AK Shukla (Dean, MGIMS)
